blocks.subtitle: Your epigenetic clock
blocks.claim: A few drops of blood show the state in which your cellular regulation is working — and which levers can be used to influence biological age.
blocks.footer: Polaris Diagnostics Europe GmbH · Hamburg · www.polarisdx.net

blocks.caption: The principle
blocks.title: How to read this report.
blocks.lead: Your body renews itself every day: cells divide, repair DNA damage and respond to stress, nutrition, sleep and the environment. These processes leave traces in DNA methylation. From these patterns the report reads your biological age — not in calendar years, but in the state of your cellular regulation.

cards.title: Protection
cards.text: How stably your DNA is protected and how efficiently the repair mechanisms work. Markers: telomeres, LINE-1.

cards.title: Regulation
cards.text: How controlled inflammatory processes remain and how resilient the cellular balance is. Marker: IL-6.

cards.title: Interpretation
cards.text: How your values compare with a reference group matched for age, sex and ethnicity.

flow.title: Measure
flow.text: Dried blood spot card, fingertip. Telomere length and methylation markers (LINE-1, IL-6, ageing markers). No fasting required.

flow.title: Interpret
flow.text: Comparison with the reference group. 100 % corresponds to the methylation value of the healthy control group.

flow.title: Change
flow.text: For every marker the matching intervention — what specifically to eat, to avoid or to change — plus follow-up monitoring.

blocks.scaleTitle: How do I read the scale?
blocks.scaleLead: All markers are given as a percentage of the reference. 100 % is the normal range, and higher is better. Telomere length is additionally reported in kilobase pairs (kbp).

scaleZones.label: 90–100 % · Amber
scaleZones.text: Action needed, counteract in a targeted way.

scaleZones.label: From 100 % · Green
scaleZones.text: No action needed, maintain the result.

blocks.caption: Biological age
blocks.title: Marker-specific age in comparison
blocks.lead: Chronological age: 48 years. Each marker yields its own biological age — an overall combined value is deliberately not calculated.
blocks.note: The dashed line marks the chronological age of 48 years. To the left of it: younger than chronological. To the right of it: older.

items.name: Telomeres
items.intro: Protective structures at the ends of the chromosomes. If they shorten too much, cells lose their ability to divide — a central driver of biological ageing.
items.text: Your telomere length is 4 % below the expected value for your age (108 instead of 112 kbp). This gives a biological telomere age of 53 years, five years above the chronological age. Together with LINE-1 this is the focus of this report; the assessment is always made in the context of the remaining markers.

rows: Because of the selenium, no more than 3–4 nuts

items.name: Epigenetic ageing markers
items.intro: The methylation of strongly age-related genes, compared with a control group matched for age, sex and ethnicity.
items.text: Slightly above the expected range — a favourable epigenetic profile. The biological age derived from this is 45 years, three years below the chronological age.

rows: Not after 2 p.m. — may disturb sleep

items.name: LINE-1
items.intro: LINE-1 elements make up around 17 % of the genome. Their methylation is regarded as a marker of global DNA regulation and thus of overall genomic stability.
items.text: Slightly reduced global DNA regulation, to be assessed within the overall profile. The derived biological age is 50 years. This marker depends on the same metabolic pathway as the telomeres — both respond to the same methyl donors.

rows: Leafy vegetables, pulses, eggs, nuts, sesame, soya
Take folate, B2, B6 and B12 together
Stabilises blood sugar, lowers oxidative burden

items.name: IL-6
items.intro: Interleukin-6 is a central messenger substance of inflammation regulation. What is assessed is the DNA methylation of IL-6-associated gene regions — not the acute blood level.
items.text: Indicates stable regulation of IL-6 activity — the best value in your profile. Here the recommendations serve maintenance, not correction.

rows: Adipose tissue is a central source of pro-inflammatory messenger substances
Grape skins, raspberry seeds, blueberries, peanuts

blocks.caption: Baseline assessment
blocks.title: Nutrition and lifestyle habits.
blocks.lead: The radar shows how close your current habits are to the scientific reference values. The further out a factor lies, the more favourable — 10 is optimal.

scores.label: Nutrition
scores.text: Good nutrient combination, room for improvement in the details.

scores.label: Lifestyle
scores.text: Balanced, with room for more exercise and stress reduction.

notices: Stress (4 out of 10) is the weakest factor and lies below the reference group. Chronic stress acts via the cortisol axis directly on inflammation and methylation markers.
Snacks and meat (5 each) are at the level of the reference group — this is where the greatest untapped potential for the telomere and LINE-1 values lies.
Tobacco (9), fruit and vegetables (8) and fluid intake (8) are clearly above average and support the good values for IL-6 and the ageing markers.
blocks.note: A baseline assessment, not an individual diagnosis. In the case of illness or during special phases of life, please have larger dietary changes supervised by a doctor.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.title: Your two focus areas.
blocks.lead: Two of your four markers are in the green range and should stay there. Two are at 96 % — and both depend on the same metabolic pathway. This results in a remarkably simple plan.

focuses.title: Methyl donors — the common denominator of telomeres and LINE-1
focuses.text: Telomeres 96 % (biologically 53 yrs) and LINE-1 96 % (biologically 50 yrs) are the two values requiring action. Both are regulated via the same nutrients: folate, vitamin B2, B6, B12 and methionine. Six of the thirteen recommendations in this report target exactly that. Specifically: two handfuls of green leafy vegetables daily, raw or briefly steamed. Eggs, cheese or fermented foods daily. 2–3 Brazil nuts. Plus at least 30 g of fibre and 3–4 cups of green tea, not with iron-rich meals.

focuses.title: Stress — the weakest lifestyle factor
focuses.text: At 4 out of 10, stress is the only factor that lies clearly below the reference group. Via the cortisol axis it acts on exactly those markers that require action in your case. The nutrition part is already solid at 72/100 — the greater effect lies here. In addition: everyday activity (6) and exercise (7) have room to grow; 30 minutes daily also supports the IL-6 value.

blocks.keepText: IL-6 at 108 % and the epigenetic ageing markers at 103 % are within the normal range. The recommendations for these two markers serve maintenance. Tobacco (9/10), fruit and vegetables (8/10) and fluid intake (8/10) support this result — nothing needs to change here.
controlItems: A follow-up measurement is useful after 4 to 6 months at the earliest — before that, changes in the methylation markers cannot be measured reliably.
From the second measurement onwards, the measured trend is reported for each marker.
For follow-up monitoring, sample collection and time of day should remain comparable.

blocks.title: Questions about your report?
blocks.text: Discuss the results with the facility that carried out the sample collection. That is where the clinical context needed for interpretation is available.

legal.title: Sample report
legal.text: All values and personal details in this document are fictitious and serve solely to illustrate the report format. This is not a real report.

legal.title: Interpretation
legal.text: This report is not a diagnosis and does not replace medical advice. The biological age reported is a model value derived from epigenetic markers, not a statement about life expectancy or disease risk. Markers describe a momentary state and are to be assessed in the individual clinical context by qualified specialists.
